title: Copilot connectors: how does outside data reach Copilot, and who can see it?
summary: Hold: the page gives conflicting assurances about source permissions, saying only source-authorised users see indexed items while also describing a setting that exposes them to everyone. Most controls and licensing statements are supported, but the account of custom federated connectors and write-tool approval also needs qualification.

claims.where: What it is: federated identity; Risks and limits: write tools
claims.claim: Federated connectors access data and perform actions using the user's source-system identity and permissions.
claims.quote: Actions run in the third-party service on behalf of the user and are limited by that user's permissions.

claims.claim: Federated connectors use OAuth 2.0.
claims.quote: Secure by design; federated access respects source permissions and authentication (OAuth 2.0).
claims.fix: Replace 'using the signed-in user's identity and OAuth 2.0' with 'using the user's identity and permissions for authenticated sources'. The custom setup page at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/set-up-custom-federated-connectors separately documents Microsoft Entra SSO, OAuth 2.0 and No Auth, unlike the overview's general wording.

claims.fix: Replace the approval wording in both sections with 'initially require user approval; users can select Allow for conversation or Always allow for an individual tool'. The cited overview's Confirm an action section documents these exceptions to repeated confirmation.

claims.where: What it is: source permissions; Why it matters
claims.claim: The unconditional claim that only source-authorised users see indexed items conflicts with the page's Visible to everyone permission option.
claims.quote: Search and Copilot show an item only to users who have access in the source. / its permissions are either source ACLs or visible to everyone
claims.fix: Replace the unconditional sentence in What it is with 'When Only people with access to this data source is selected, the connector respects source ACLs; Visible to everyone grants access to all users in the organisation.' This is the distinction at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/manage-access-permissions.

claims.claim: The sources omit the custom federated setup page needed to disclose conflicting Microsoft guidance about custom support and authentication.

claims.fix: Add 'Set up custom federated connectors' at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/set-up-custom-federated-connectors to sources. This is the single consolidated finding for additional Microsoft pages relied on during this check.
